title: Fermix management socket protocol
description: Packet-4 framed JSON wire contract between the Fermix daemon and the Fermix macOS application. Source of truth: FermixCore.Management.Protocol. See PROTOCOL.md.

x-plugin-vocabulary.description: The closed sets a plugin row draws on. Published so a reader can enumerate them and a support log can be searched by status; a client renders `status_sentence` and `primary_verb` and never switches on those words — it switches on `primary_action` and `actions`, which name the method each button runs.

result.description: A response carries no method, so the result shape is selected by the method of the correlated request rather than discriminated from the envelope alone.

minimum_versions.description: The minimum protocol version of every method this daemon serves, keyed by method name. Added in v2; absent on a v1 daemon, which serves every method it lists at version 1.

restart_reasons.description: Boot-bound sections waiting on a restart, by name. Added in v2; absent on a v1 daemon, where the client renders the plain restart sentence with no reason list.

remediation.description: What to do about this check, in the daemon's own words. Added in v2; absent or null on a v1 daemon, where the client renders the summary with no action button.

settingValue.description: One row value: a public scalar, a list of strings, or null. Null is a value with a meaning rather than an absent field, so it is written rather than omitted.

settingsRow.description: Every field is always present, null where it does not apply, so a client decodes a fixed record rather than probing for keys.

present.description: Whether a credential sits at this key's own path. Null on every kind but secret; a secret row never carries a value.

options.description: The value space of a choice row, unless `suggestions` is true, in which case it is only what a client may offer inline.

read_only.description: A row this section publishes that settings.apply will not take, rendered as a plain labelled row rather than a control whose save always refuses.

suggestions.description: Whether this choice row's options are only what a client may offer inline rather than its whole value space. True on the time zone and communication style rows, where a native picker may send any value the daemon validates; false everywhere else, and settings.apply then refuses a value that is not among the options. False on every non-choice kind.

unit.description: What a number counts, rendered beside the field. Null where the number counts nothing but itself, and on every non-number row.

format.description: How a number reads: a plain count, a 0-1 fraction as a percentage, whole cents as money, or a duration. Null on every other kind.

side_effects.description: Changes the operator did not type, in the daemon's own sentences.

jobKind.description: The long operation a job runs. One shape covers every family, so a client writes one poller rather than one per operation.

jobStatus.description: The job's state. `phase` is display copy for the current step and is never switched on; this is the state.

jobFailure.description: Why a job ended badly, in the daemon's own words. The sentence is rendered; a client never composes one from the code.

jobView.description: Every field is always present, null where it does not apply. A terminal job clears `phase` unless it failed or timed out, where the step it stopped in is part of the diagnosis.

result.description: The job's own answer, flat and bounded: public scalars only.

providers_models_list_result.description: A live listing never degrades to the catalog: a live fetch that fails answers `unavailable`, so `source` always names where these rows came from.

auth_start_result.description: The job view plus the authorize url the daemon minted. Both extra fields are returned once, on the call that starts the flow; a later read of the same job carries the job view alone.

pluginSetting.description: One value the plugin's manifest declares, with the label the manifest wrote for it.

pluginAccessProfile.description: One access level the manifest offers. `write` is the daemon's own flag: a client warns on it rather than reading a scope out of the label. The manifest validator requires a non-empty display name on every profile, so the label is never null.

pluginOAuthClient.description: A sign-in client the operator registered. client_id is its public identifier; secret_present reports credential presence independently from configured. The secret value is never returned. The added fields are optional for older protocol-2 engines. A null redirect_port selects the daemon's default.

pluginAction.description: Which method a plugin row's button runs. Closed: a client that meets an unknown id draws no button rather than guessing one.

pluginRow.description: One integration, in the daemon's own words. Every field is always present, null where it does not apply, and both halves of the union (installed and not yet installed) publish this one shape. A null `runtime_kind` is the http rail, which runs inside Fermix itself; `consent_sentence` says so in words and is never absent.

auth_provider.description: The sign-in family this plugin belongs to, which is the `oauth_clients` entry its detail carries. Null on a plugin that needs no client.

primary_verb.description: The one verb the row leads with. Null where the next step is not a button this surface owns, so the client uses its own word rather than a daemon word naming something else.

primary_action.description: Which method the leading verb runs, from a closed set. A word is not a routing key: paint `primary_verb` and route on this. Null exactly when `primary_verb` is null.

actions.description: One action id per entry in `verbs`, in the same order, saying which method that button runs.

credential_present.description: Whether a credential sits behind this plugin. Published rather than inferred from `account_label`, which a plugin authenticating with a typed token never has.

workspaces.description: What the last discovery on this daemon found. Empty until one has run, and cleared by a restart.

plugins_workspace_select_start_params.description: An unnamed workspace is a display problem rather than a configuration error, so the label may be empty; the identifier may not.

plugins_oauth_client_set_params.description: The client secret is not a parameter: it arrives through `secret.set` under `oauth_client:<provider>`. An absent redirect port clears any override and leaves the daemon's own default in force.

plugins_setting_set_params.description: A manifest-declared setting is text: the daemon refuses any other value rather than coercing one.

computer_use_permissions_get_result.description: `installed` comes from the installer rather than from the probe: the feature being switched off says nothing about whether the helper is on disk.
